text: Check reachability, the watchdog's records and the modem's state.
The modem is OPERATIONAL, the watchdog has hit its reload cap, and sending fails with 'No buffer space available'. Look at the kernel messages for the WAN NIC.
vtnet0 shows repeated transmit watchdog timeouts and climbing output errors: the driver is hung. Reloads cannot reset it; a reboot of the firewall does.

arguments.reason: The WAN NIC driver (vtnet0) is hung: transmit watchdog timeouts, output errors climbing, sends fail with No buffer space available. 12 reloads in 24 h (the cap) did not help and the modem is OPERATIONAL. Only a reboot resets the driver.

arguments.cause: The firewall's WAN network driver (vtnet0) has hung: its transmit queue times out, so nothing can be sent to the provider even though the modem is registered and healthy.
evidence: gw.lan: ping to the provider's gateway fails with sendto: No buffer space available
gw.lan: dmesg shows repeated vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0; netstat -i shows 48211 output errors on vtnet0
gw.lan: events.jsonl shows 12 reloads in 24 hours, the cap, with no effect; modem-metrics.jsonl shows OPERATIONAL since 02:29
arguments.recommendation: Reboot the firewall to reset the WAN driver (requested as firewall_reboot). Do not reboot the modem; it is healthy. If timeouts return after the reboot, investigate the virtual NIC on the hypervisor.
